newsitem.title: USA: Jury selection under way in Florida tobacco lawsuit.
newsitem.headline: Jury selection under way in Florida tobacco lawsuit.

text.p: Jury selection began Friday in Florida's billion-dollar lawsuit against the tobacco industry to recover the cost of treating sick smokers.
The landmark case, which has the attention of legal scholars and financial markets, is the first state lawsuit against the major cigarette makers to go to trial.

Palm Beach Circuit Judge Harold Cohen, in a 20-minute address, told a 300-member jury pool that "the state alleges that the defendants were negligent and that they manufactured a dangerous and defective product."
Jurors were to be given a questionnaire before individual questioning of the prospective panel members begins next week. Six jurors and nine alternates will be selected for the trial.

Florida Gov. Lawton Chiles, the named plaintiff in the lawsuit, and Attorney General Bob Butterworth attended the opening session, sending a murmur through the jury pool when they walked into the room.

"This is the first time the American public is going to find out the full truth about what the tobacco companies have been doing, what they've been hiding for the past 40 years," Butterworth said outside the courthouse before trial began.
